newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Jan 11 Initial Claims from 323,000, Jan 4 from 355,000; Jan 11 4-Week Average from 348,750, Jan 4 from 355,500; Jan 4 Continued Claims from 2,714,000 and Dec 28 from 2,519,000.
Wall Street economists had forcast initial jobless claims of 347,000 in the January 18 week.
The department said 29 states and Puerto Rico reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended January 11, the latest period for which data are available.

Among the largest were Ohio, with 11,329 new claims filings; North Carolina, with 11,269; Georgia, with 11,085; Tennessee, with 10,644; Pennsylvania, with 8,432; Illinois, with 7,781; and Alabama, with 7,086.

Ohio attributed the increase to holiday shutdowns in various industries. North Carolina had layoffs in the textile, apparel, furniture, rubber, non-electrical machinery and electrical equipment industries.
Labor said four states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the January 11 week.

They were New York, with 11,966 fewer filings; Michigan, with 8,365; Arkansas, with 3,155; and Indiana, with 1,265. Michigan reported fewer layoffs in a variety of industries, while Arkansas had fewer layoffs in the non-electrical machinery industry.
